At H1, we believe access to the best healthcare information is a basic human right. Our mission is to provide a platform that can optimally inform every doctor interaction globally. This promotes health equity and builds needed trust in healthcare systems. To accomplish this, our teams harness the power of data and AI-technology to unlock groundbreaking medical insights and convert those insights into action that result in optimal patient outcomes and accelerates an equitable and inclusive drug development lifecycle. Visit h1.com to learn more about us.

As part of H1’s hiring process, all candidates are required to participate in an in-person final interview. Depending on your location, this may require travel.

H1's Product Engineering organization is the engine behind the products that put our data in front of the people who need it most, health plans, digital health companies, life sciences organizations, and the clinical teams they serve. We build the client-facing products, APIs, integrations, and intelligent workflows that transform H1's rich underlying data into real decisions: which providers belong in a network directory, where clinical trials should run, and how healthcare organizations can operate with greater accuracy and trust. Product Engineering at H1 sits at the crossroads of complex data systems and enterprise software delivery, and our work directly drives revenue, client retention, and patient impact. We move fast, we own our products end-to-end, and we hold ourselves to a high bar — because in healthcare, the quality of what we build has consequences.

What You'll Do At H1

As a Director of Software Engineering at H1, you will own a high-impact product engineering domain and lead the team responsible for the client-facing products, integrations, and workflows within it. You will set the technical vision, build and develop your team, co-own the product roadmap with the PM, and serve as the trusted engineering voice across sales, customer success, and the broader organization. You will operate with real accountability; for delivery, for your people, and for the business outcomes that depend on your domain performing at its best.

You will:

Lead, grow, and develop a high-performing product engineering team; hiring, coaching, performance management, and building a culture where engineers do their best work
Partner with Product Management to co-own the roadmap, translating client needs and business priorities into a clear engineering strategy and delivery plan
Set technical direction; architecture standards, agentic workflow practices, and the bar for what good looks like — while staying close enough to engage meaningfully in system design decisions with your team
Own delivery accountability for your segment: on-time, high-quality releases that meet client SLAs
Run the engineering operating rhythm, manage on-call schedules, sprint planning, triage outages, retrospectives, and incident reviews, with structure and consistency
Manage competing priorities across Customer Support, sales, PM, and engineering, communicating tradeoffs clearly and making calls when the path isn't obvious
Serve as the senior engineering voice in cross-functional conversations; occasionally engaging directly with clients as a subject matter expert, though your primary surface is internal
Own multiple product lines simultaneously, bringing prioritization and clarity across a growing portfolio

About You

You are a seasoned engineering leader who has built and shipped SaaS products in complex data environments, and you know the difference between owning a product and managing a team that builds one. You take genuine pride in your people: you invest in them, challenge them, and measure your success by how they grow. You are comfortable at the intersection of engineering and business, equally capable of walking a client through how your product works and walking your engineers through a hard architectural tradeoff. You don't need to be writing code every day, but you stay close to the technology, you have a clear answer for how you use modern tooling and agentic workflows to stay effective, you understand how data moves through a system, and your engineers trust that when you weigh in on a technical decision, it's grounded in real understanding. You thrive in environments where priorities shift, ambiguity is constant, and the expectation is that you build the structure rather than wait for it. You are a clear communicator, a decisive decision-maker, and the kind of leader people point to when asked who made them better.

Proven track record owning a SaaS product end-to-end in a complex data environment, from technical architecture through client delivery and operations.
Experience managing multiple product lines simultaneously with a clear approach to prioritization and keeping teams unblocked.
Backend product engineering background: APIs, client-facing integrations, data-driven product surfaces, and visualization layers, this is not a data pipeline, infrastructure, or ML role.

Strong communicator across audiences; executives, sales leaders, engineers, and clients, and a trusted technical voice in commercial conversations

Raise the standard of the work over time

$230,000 - $290,000

10+ years of software engineering experience, including significant leadership experience managing engineering teams and Tech Leads/managers
Track record of developing talent and raising team performance over time

Hire, develop, and lead engineers and managers.
Hire, develop, and lead engineers and managers.

What You Own

Technical Leadership

Security reviews of product and infrastructure changes, plus carrier and vendor security questionnaires and audits
Serving as the technical point of contact and leader with key partners

Engineering Management

Vendor and AI Management

Owning and evolving Pawlicy's AI policy and best practices. Lead the company's rollout and expansion of AI usage while optimizing cost.

Where You Partner

OKRs: creation and ownership of key business goals and objectives
Product: sprint priorities, tech debt vs feature velocity tradeoffs, and delivery timelines with the senior product manager and the Chief Product Officer
Design: front end quality and design QA with the senior product designer
Partnerships and legal: carrier and vendor security questionnaires, audits, and integration requirements
Data and analytics: tooling and reliable data flow across product systems

What Success Looks Like

First 90 days

Delivery is stable and predictable: releases ship on a defined cadence, and incidents have owners, escalation paths, and postmortems
Full command of the architecture: the site, quote engine, and carrier integrations, with a prioritized view of technical debt and risk
1:1s and career development running for every engineer
A first version of Pawlicy's AI development policy and best practices in place

First 12 months

A technical roadmap has been executed with security investments sequenced against business priorities
Delivery measurably improved: velocity, quality, and production stability all trend the right way
Carrier and vendor security reviews handled end to end without external help
Engineers are growing against clear development plans, and the team is confident in the technical bar you set
AI-assisted development is ingrained in the culture and adopted with measured results

Requirements

10+ years of software engineering experience, including 5+ years managing engineers and 2+ years in a senior engineering leadership role (Director, or senior-most technical leader), ideally at an early stage startup or fast-moving environment
The stack: TypeScript, Next.js, Node, GraphQL, Postgres, AWS
Proven technical ownership and leadership: you have owned the technical strategy, architecture, and roadmap for a production consumer product, and built or scaled the team that delivered it
Still hands-on: comfortable reviewing PRs, reading code deeply, and jumping into an incident
Experience with application security and third-party compliance: security reviews, vendor questionnaires, and audits
Track record of excellent cross department communication and relationships leading to business success
Practical enthusiasm for AI-assisted development
Legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship
Preferred: experience in insurance or fintech, or with partner API integrations.

How You Work

You set your own technical agenda: there is no CTO above you defining priorities, and you generate the roadmap rather than execute one handed down
You fix things nobody asked you to fix: architecture, process, or tooling.
You enjoy teaching non-technical colleagues and working with cross functional teams
You push back, disagree, and align without it becoming political
You lead from the front with AI tool adoption and usage and evangelize across the company

AI and the Hiring Process

Company Overview

Performance Contracting Group is a national employee-owned specialty contractor that offers quality services and products to the commercial, industrial, and non-residential construction markets. We are committed to recruiting, developing, and advancing employees from a diversity of backgrounds and experiences, as well as supporting a culture of safety and inclusiveness that allows you to contribute to your fullest potential. We place high value on training and professional development, encouraging you to broaden and strengthen your unique skill sets so you can fully realize your potential.

The Director, IT Engineering provides enterprise leadership for the software, data, integration, and Microsoft Dynamics 365 capabilities that enable PCG’s business operations. The role is accountable for designing, building, integrating, modernizing, and sustaining secure, scalable, and reliable solutions. This leader establishes disciplined engineering practices, clear ownership, and outcome-based roadmaps that accelerate business value while improving quality, maintainability and cost effectiveness.

Leadership Mandate

Build an integrated enterprise engineering capability with persistent ownership of custom software, business applications, enterprise data pipelines and products, APIs and integrations, and the Microsoft Dynamics 365 platform. Set direction, establish operating expectations, and ensure internal teams and partners are accountable for measurable business outcomes, technical quality, secure delivery, operational readiness, and sustainable lifecycle management.

Strategic Outcomes

Faster delivery of business capabilities through modern software engineering, reusable components, automation, and clear alignment to enterprise priorities.
Clear ownership and outcome-based roadmaps for custom software, Microsoft Dynamics 365, enterprise data products, APIs, and integrations.
Reliable, secure, and maintainable applications supported by consistent architecture, development, testing, release, monitoring, and support practices.
Trusted, governed, and reusable enterprise data that enables reporting, analytics, automation, AI, and better operational decisions.
A simplified integration environment that reduces point-to-point interfaces, improves data flow, and connects Dynamics 365 with core enterprise and field systems.
A high-performing engineering organization with strong technical leadership, talent development, financial discipline, and accountability for business outcomes.

Key Accountabilities

Engineering Strategy & Operating Model: Publish and maintain a rolling 18–24-month roadmap for software, data, integration, and Dynamics 365 capabilities; review priorities, capacity, dependencies, risks, and expected business outcomes with technology and business leaders at least quarterly.
Software Engineering: Ensure 100% of actively developed applications have an accountable owner, documented architecture, product backlog, support model, security classification, lifecycle status, and measurable service objectives. Establish automated build, test, security, and deployment controls for all material production releases.
Microsoft Dynamics 365 Engineering: Own the platform roadmap, solution architecture, configuration, extensions, Power Platform components, security roles, integrations, data, release calendar, and partner delivery. Review customizations quarterly and require documented business justification, ownership, testing, and lifecycle plans for all approved extensions.
Data Engineering: Assign accountable owners and service measures to all critical data products and pipelines. Monitor data quality, freshness, availability, lineage, security, and failed processing daily; maintain remediation plans for measures below target.
Integration & API Engineering: Maintain a current inventory of production APIs, interfaces, events, owners, dependencies, service levels, and lifecycle status. Review integration health monthly and deliver an annual plan to retire redundant or unsupported point-to-point interfaces.
Engineering Quality & Operations: Set and report monthly measures for delivery lead time, deployment frequency, failed changes, production defects, availability, incident recovery, automated test coverage, vulnerabilities, and recurring incidents. Require documented production-readiness approval before release.
Architecture, Security & Governance Partnership: Ensure 100% of material solutions complete required architecture, security, data governance, resiliency, and operational reviews before production approval; track exceptions to an accountable owner and target resolution date.
Talent & Culture: Maintain workforce and succession plans for critical roles, complete quarterly talent reviews, establish annual development objectives for all team members, and reduce single-person dependencies through documented cross-training and coverage plans.

Translate business priorities and operational needs into clear software, Dynamics 365, data, and integration strategies, roadmaps, investment decisions, and executable plans.
Create clarity around solution ownership, engineering decision rights, service boundaries, data stewardship, integration responsibilities, technical standards, escalation paths, and definitions of done.
Balance delivery speed with security, reliability, maintainability, user experience, cost, and long-term enterprise architecture.
Engage business stakeholders early, frame operational problems before selecting solutions, and favor standard Dynamics 365 capabilities where they meet business needs before introducing customization.
Communicate complex engineering topics in plain business language and provide transparent visibility into delivery, capacity, risk, quality, cost, technical debt, and realized value.
Develop a leadership bench and career pathways that strengthen critical software, data, integration, and Dynamics 365 capabilities and reduce key-person dependency.

Basic Qualifications

Minimum of 10 years of senior technology leadership experience, including a proven track record of building and leading multidisciplinary engineering organizations within complex, distributed enterprise environments.
Demonstrated success leading software engineering, data engineering, integration and API engineering, and enterprise business application delivery.
Significant experience governing and delivering Microsoft Dynamics 365 solutions, including configuration, extensions, Power Platform, security, data, integrations, release management, and implementation partners.
Experience establishing durable solution ownership, outcome-based roadmaps, engineering standards, governance, budgets, capacity models, and measurable performance outcomes.
Strong knowledge of modern software delivery, cloud and hybrid architectures, automated testing and deployment, APIs, event-driven integration, data platforms, observability, secure development, and automation.
Experience modernizing legacy applications, data pipelines, and integrations while managing technical debt and minimizing business disruption.
Strong executive communication and business partnership skills, including the ability to translate technical choices, risk, capacity, cost, and debt into business impact and investment decisions.
Experience leading internal teams, contractors, managed services, and strategic vendors while developing leaders and technical talent.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in computer science, software engineering, information systems, data engineering, business, or a related field. Relevant Microsoft Dynamics 365, Power Platform, cloud, data, integration, or leadership certifications are preferred.

new_jobs.title: Director Cloud Engineering
new_jobs.description:
ComPsych Ⓡ is the worldwide leader in organizational mental health, well-being, and absence management, dedicated to igniting human potential in workplaces across the globe. For over 40 years, we have combined the best in technology with unmatched human expertise to help individuals and their organizations thrive. Our GuidanceResources Ⓡ and AbsenceResources Ⓡ solutions deliver end-to-end mental health, well-being, work-life, health navigation, and absence support to more than 75,000 customers worldwide, touching more than 160 million lives across 200 countries. Visit compsych.com to find out why 40% of the Fortune 500 choose ComPsych for their mental health and absence management needs.

About The Role

ComPsych is building out its Cloud Engineering function as we move from traditional, on-premise IT to a modern, cloud-native platform the whole organization builds on. We treat the platform as a product: an internal developer portal, CI/CD pipelines, paved roads, tooling, automation, and guardrails that let every team build, ship, and run their software securely and fast. Cloud migration and modernization are part of the journey, but the mission is the platform itself.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You lead the Cloud Engineering function and stay technically credible, setting strategy, standards, and direction and building alongside a very talented Lead/Architect and your team, not directing from a distance. AI isn't a side project here, it's how we build and operate the platform: your team uses AI to build tools, pipelines, and automation, and you set the bar for directing and validating what it produces. Our platform carries behavioral health data for millions of members, so reliability, security, and cost aren't competing conversations, they're the same one.

What You'll Do

You own the Cloud Engineering function end to end. Partnering with a very talented Lead/Architect and your team, you set the strategy, standards, and direction, and stay hands-on enough to be credible, delivering the platform, the pipelines, the tooling, and the guardrails the rest of the organization builds on.

Build the internal developer portal and self-service platform. A service catalog, golden paths, paved roads, and developer experience that let product teams provision, build, deploy, and run their software securely without waiting on you.
Own CI/CD pipelines, platform tools, and solutions. The pipelines, templates, SDKs, and platform services the function ships, built for reuse across every team, coding them hands-on and directing AI to accelerate.
Build and support ComPsych DevSecOps and Cloud Engineering Strategy. Secure CI/CD (SAST/DAST/SCA, secrets and image scanning), Infrastructure-as-Code, and policy-as-code guardrails, with security built into the pipeline and shift-left adopted across teams.
Own the cloud foundation the platform runs on. Landing zones and a Cloud Center of Excellence (CCoE), reference architectures, and reliability and cost as first-class engineering (SLOs, observability, resilience, and FinOps).
Enable AI and data at the platform layer. The environments, pipelines, and guardrails that let the business build and run AI/ML and GenAI safely and at scale, making AI and automation the platform's default.
Govern responsible and secure AI. Beyond enabling AI/ML and GenAI, set the guardrails and governance for its safe use across Cloud Engineering: acceptable-use and model/data governance, protection against insecure AI-generated code, and alignment to AI risk frameworks (NIST AI RMF, OWASP LLM Top 10, ISO 42001).
Own compliance and audit-readiness across Cloud Engineering. Make continuous compliance, control mapping, and automated audit evidence a platform capability every team inherits; own third-party and open-source risk, and partner with Security and GRC to keep the function aligned to HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2, NIST, ISO 27001, and GDPR.
Ensure data protection, privacy, and data residency by design. Encryption and key management, least-privilege access to PHI/ePHI, privacy-by-design, and residency-aware landing zones and region placement so workloads and data live where each jurisdiction requires across our domestic and international footprint.
Lead the function and the team. Evolve legacy infrastructure into cloud-native services where it serves the platform, establish the Cloud Engineering function, hire and reskill talent, set standards, and manage vendors, tooling, and budget.

What We're Looking For

You've built a platform, not just managed one. You've delivered developer-facing platform capabilities (an internal developer portal, CI/CD, paved roads, and tooling) and can point to teams that shipped faster and safer because of what you built.
You're hands-on and deeply technical. Multi-cloud (AWS, Azure), Infrastructure-as-Code and configuration management (Terraform, Ansible), containers, and secure CI/CD are things you still build, not just oversee, and AI is your primary surface for building them.
You run platforms like products, with self-service, golden paths, and an internal developer portal that scale across many teams.
You build and support a DevSecOps practice: shift-left security, policy-as-code, and secrets/IAM/RBAC built into the pipeline. In a system that carries behavioral health data, “secure” and “shipped” are the same bar.
You own reliability and cost and enable AI and data, with SRE (SLOs, observability, incident response) and FinOps as core disciplines and a point of view on responsible AI enablement.
You govern AI as well as enable it. A point of view on responsible, secure AI, model and data governance, guarding against insecure AI-generated code, and AI risk frameworks (NIST AI RMF, OWASP LLM Top 10, ISO 42001).
You build compliance into the platform, not around it. Continuous compliance, control mapping, and automated audit evidence, plus third-party and open-source risk, in a regulated environment (HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2, NIST, ISO 27001, GDPR).
You lead data protection and residency. Encryption and key management, least-privilege to sensitive data (PHI/ePHI), privacy-by-design, and multi-region data-residency placement across domestic and international operations.
You lead by building alongside your team, leading and working with your team, establishing a foundation of technology and quality excellence, reskilling talent, and communicating clearly to engineers and executives. Credentials: 10+ years in cloud, platform, or infrastructure engineering with team leadership; Bachelor's in Computer Science or a related field; cloud certifications (AWS or Azure Solutions Architect / DevOps / SRE) strongly preferred.

Compensation And Benefits

Full benefits package, including Paid Time Off (PTO), medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with match, robust EAP, wellness program, and much more

We're building a workplace where employees can grow their careers, make an impact, and help shape the future of telecommunications across Arizona. Position Summary

The Sr. Director of Design & Engineering – Fiber to the Home (FTTH) at Wecom Fiber is a senior leadership role responsible for overseeing the full lifecycle of outside plant (OSP) network design, engineering, and deployment readiness across our expanding FTTH footprint. This strategic position involves leading and managing a team of CAD drafters, GIS specialists, OSP engineers, and design professionals to ensure the successful delivery of high-quality fiber network designs in the telecommunications industry. The Director will translate Wecom's fiber expansion strategy into actionable engineering plans, own design standards and quality assurance, and serve as the senior technical voice across construction, operations, permitting, and executive leadership.

Strategic Leadership & Program Execution

Translate Wecom's FTTH expansion strategy into actionable, scalable engineering plans aligned with long-range forecasts and business objectives.
Own the technical vision for all Outside Plant (OSP) design, GPON/XGS-PON architecture, and last-mile delivery infrastructure.
Develop and continuously refine companywide engineering standards, design guidelines, and quality benchmarks for FTTH network builds.
Track and report major milestones across design, permitting, construction, and activation stages of the fiber build lifecycle.
Oversee BEAD-funded projects, ensuring compliance milestones, required documentation, and federal, state, and subgrant reporting requirements are completed accurately and on schedule.
Identify and champion opportunities for process automation, GIS/CAD toolset adoption, and workflow optimization to reduce cycle times and improve deliverable quality.

Network Design & Engineering Quality

Oversee quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) programs for internal and vendor-produced designs, ensuring accurate cable records and GIS asset data.

Vice President, Software Engineering

Mastercard Send, part of the Mastercard Move portfolio, powers near real-time money movement to billions of cards, bank, and digital accounts worldwide. The platform enables financial institutions, fintechs, businesses, and digital partners to deliver fast, secure, and reliable payment experiences across domestic and cross-border use cases.

We are seeking a Vice President, Software Engineering to lead the strategy, architecture, delivery, and operation of the Mastercard Send engineering organization. This role partners closely with Product, Operations, Security, Risk, and other technology leaders to deliver secure, reliable, and scalable solutions that support Mastercard's global payments ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

Software Architecture & Engineering Excellence

Live experiences help people cross today’s digital divide and focus on what truly connects us – the here, the now, this once-in-a-lifetime moment that’s bringing us together. To fulfill Gametime’s mission of uniting the world through shared experiences, we make it easy for people to discover and access the live experiences that matter most.

With platforms on iOS, Android, mobile web and desktop supporting more than 60,000 events across the US and Canada, we are reimagining the event ticket industry in order to move at the speed of life.

The Role

Gametime’s Fan Experience team owns how fans discover, decide on, and purchase tickets on the demand side of our marketplace — the core experience for millions of ticket buyers across iOS, Android, mobile web, and desktop. This Engineering Manager
will lead a team of full-stack and front-end engineers building the features and value propositions that define how fans experience Gametime, partnering day-to-day with a dedicated Product Manager and Designer to move quickly from idea to production.

This is a hands-on role. You’ll spend real time on the keyboard alongside your team, and you’ll set the standard for how the team uses frontier models, AI coding tools, and new harnesses to generate, review, test, and monitor code — raising both velocity and quality as the bar for what’s possible keeps moving. This role reports to the VP of Product.

What You’ll Do

Hands-on leadership: spend a meaningful share of your time actually coding alongside the team — you lead from the front, not just from the roadmap
AI-forward engineering: set the standard for how your team uses frontier models, AI coding agents/harnesses, and new tooling to generate, review, test, and monitor code — the primary lever for increasing velocity and quality (i.e. fewer bugs, more stable services, cohesive system architecture) together, not as a trade-off
Cross-functional partnership: partner closely, day-to-day, with a dedicated PM and Designer as a trio; bring a real point of view on what the product and features should be, not just how to build them
Velocity investment: partner with product to identify and invest in what will let the team move faster over time — tooling, domain foundation design, tech debt paydown, and better use of AI in the development loop
Risk partnership: partner with product to surface the risks in what’s being proposed, and bring concrete recommendations and proposals for how to mitigate and eliminate those risks over time
Delivery: own the engineering roadmap and execution plan for your area, balancing speed, quality, and technical debt
Mentorship and talent bar: mentor engineers toward their next career level, hold a high talent bar for hiring and performance on your team, and help level up talent on other teams too
Cross-team technical leadership: partner with engineering leads and counterparts on other teams to improve the marketplace more broadly, technically, over time
A team and roadmap tied directly to fan-facing feature velocity, quality, and business outcomes on the demand side of our marketplace

What You’ll Bring

A hands-on engineering manager — comfortable spending real time writing and reviewing code alongside your team, not just directing from above
Direct experience using frontier models, AI coding agents/harnesses, and modern tooling to meaningfully improve engineering velocity and quality, and a point of view on where this is headed
A track record of shipping consumer-facing product features that moved measurable business outcomes
Strong cross-functional partnership skills — comfortable operating as a true peer to Product and Design, with your own opinions on what should be built, not just executing their specs
Experience managing full-stack and/or front-end engineering teams, with meaningful people-management experience (typically 5+ years in engineering, including several as a manager)
Familiarity with SQL/analytics to diagnose funnel and feature performance
Experience leading full-stack teams with end-to-end ownership of consumer-facing web and mobile products, backend services, and APIs in a high-traffic marketplace or e-commerce environment.
Strong understanding of modern front-end stacks (e.g., React and React Native), backend services, APIs, and full-stack architecture, with the technical depth to lead teams across the stack.
Experience partnering with Product and Design in a fast-moving, iterative environment (feature flags, A/B testing, rapid experimentation)
A data-driven approach to prioritization and technical trade-offs

Nice to Have

Experience in consumer marketplaces or high-intent, high-conversion consumer apps
A track record of building or championing internal tooling/platform investments that compounded team velocity over time

Competitive salary & equity package

As Director, Network Operations Engineering, you will lead the strategy, architecture, and operational excellence of enterprise network services that support critical business operations and client connectivity. You will be accountable for building resilient, secure, scalable, and cloud‑ready network platforms across campus, data center, colocation, hybrid, and cloud environments.

In this role, you will drive a cloud‑first, automation‑led network strategy, improve operational reliability and recovery, and strengthen governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) maturity. You will lead and grow a high‑performing team of network engineers while partnering closely with product, infrastructure, security, audit, and risk teams to ensure network services meet business, client, and regulatory expectations.

This role reports directly to Network Operations leadership.

Network Architecture & Strategy

Define and lead the design and implementation of complex enterprise network architectures, including LAN, WAN, data center, SD‑WAN, and hybrid cloud environments
Develop and execute network strategies and multi‑year roadmaps aligned with business objectives and industry best practices
Establish enterprise standards for network design, client connectivity, resiliency, and security
Evaluate emerging networking technologies and recommend solutions that improve performance, scalability, reliability, and security

Network Operations, Reliability & Performance

Own enterprise‑level network operations, ensuring availability, capacity, performance, and security across on‑prem and cloud environments
Oversee the operation of routers, switches, firewalls, load balancers, wireless infrastructure, and cloud networking services
Lead the response to complex network incidents, including root‑cause analysis and implementation of corrective and preventive actions
Reduce operational risk by improving testing practices, recovery planning, and standardization of connectivity models
Monitor network performance, utilization, and capacity; sponsor optimization initiatives such as traffic engineering and QoS

Cloud, Automation & Modernization

Lead execution of the cloud and hybrid network strategy, including hybrid connectivity, cloud networking patterns, and cost‑optimization initiatives
Drive adoption of network automation and Infrastructure as Code, leveraging tools such as Ansible, Python, and SDN technologies
Ensure network provisioning, configuration management, and change execution are automated to improve efficiency and reduce manual errors
Establish cloud‑specific operational models, including monitoring, incident management, and financial governance

Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC)

Own network‑related governance, risk, and compliance responsibilities
Standardize network documentation, controls, and audit evidence
Track audit findings, remediation actions, and control effectiveness through structured governance forums
Partner with security, risk, and audit teams to ensure ongoing regulatory readiness

Leadership, Delivery & Vendor Management

Lead, mentor, and develop a team of network operations and engineering professionals, with planned growth as demand increases
Set priorities, performance goals, and accountability across the organization
Lead network‑related programs and initiatives, including upgrades, migrations, and technology refreshes
Define project scope, timelines, resources, and budgets to ensure delivery on schedule and within constraints
Evaluate network vendors, support contract negotiations, and manage strategic vendor relationships
Ensure high‑quality network documentation, diagrams, procedures, and knowledge sharing
Communicate network risks, initiatives, and incidents effectively to senior leadership, including executive‑ready presentations (PowerPoint, Visio)

Qualifications

10+ years of experience in network engineering, operations, or infrastructure leadership roles within large, global enterprises
Demonstrated experience leading and developing technical teams
Bachelor’s degree preferred or equivalent practical experience
Experience supporting regulated or highly audited environments

Talents Needed for Success

Deep expertise in enterprise network architecture and operations
Expert‑level knowledge of networking protocols and technologies, including: - TCP/IP, OSPF, BGP, MPLS
VLAN, STP
Network security protocols (IPsec, SSL/TLS)
Strong experience with data center, hybrid, and cloud networking
Extensive experience with enterprise network devices and vendors
In‑depth understanding of network security principles, including firewalls, VPNs, IDS/IPS, and access control
Proven ability to lead incident response, root‑cause analysis, and operational improvement programs
Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder‑management skills
Demonstrated experience driving organizational process improvement and change

Nice to Have Skills

Experience with Infoblox, Guardicore, or similar network/IPAM/security platforms
Prior ownership of client connectivity platforms or services
Experience building centralized network topology or observability repositories
Advanced network certifications (CCIE, JNCIE)

We are in search of a VP of Engineering for our Channels division, the action layer of the Braze technology platform. Our channels are where the Braze platform meets the end user, where our customers create rich messaging that is delivered to their end users via our channels: Email, Push, SMS/MMS/RCS, WhatsApp, LINE, In-App Messages, Content Cards, Banners, Landing Pages, Feature Flags, Webhooks, and more to come. 
You will lead this multi-team division through its next stage of technical and product transformation. You will manage the team and help to grow the organization, leading software engineering via architecture design, growing engineering teams and skillsets, setting vision and goals, process and protocol, and hiring. On the product front - you will solve a number of interesting problems, from developing highly differentiated and sophisticated channel products, to thinking about how we build and position the broad portfolio of channels. On the engineering front - maturation of our systems into a more modular, efficient technology platform, all while delivering best-in-class product, is a major goal. And across both fronts, you will lead this organization through the AI transition: channel products that are increasingly intelligent and agentic, and an engineering org that leverages AI-assisted development to raise its own velocity and quality bar.
WHO YOU ARE

Several years of relevant experience as a manager of experienced managers with a strong track record of transformative success
A durable, motivated, ambitious, high-energy leader
A great people leader, capable of growing a world class team
A great technical leader, who can operate at different levels of granularity, from high level vision to partnering on detailed technology decisions

Fluent in AI-assisted engineering, with an informed point of view on how AI agents and tooling change the way engineering organizations build, operate, and are shaped
A great process leader, who understands when to add and remove processes to help the org execute the best it can
An excellent communicator and writer, whose impact and leadership is obvious in the artifacts they create to guide their team

Braze is the leading customer engagement platform that empowers brands to Be Absolutely Engaging™ Braze helps brands deliver great customer experiences that drive value both for consumers and for their businesses. Braze is also proudly certified as a Great Place to Work® in the U.S., the UK, Australia, and Singapore.
The company is headquartered in New York with offices in Austin, Berlin, Bucharest, Chicago, Dubai, Jakarta, London, Paris, San Francisco, São Paulo, Singapore, Seoul, Sydney and Tokyo.
BRAZE IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

new_jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence . As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe is a vertically integrated AI Factory company with a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. Our competitive advantage, "Speed is the only moat," is directly tied to our ability to rapidly design, manufacture, and deploy our own modular power and compute infrastructure.

We are seeking a Sustaining Engineering Leader to own how Spark performs after it is deployed. Product Management defines the next generation. New Product Introduction delivers it into production. You own each generation from the moment it leaves ramp: fleet reliability, field failures, configuration, obsolescence, and the design changes that keep deployed units performing for their full service life.

You do not set the roadmap and you do not run the factory. You own the installed base, and you are the evidence source Product Management and NPI both depend on. You will start as the single-threaded owner of this function and build the team as the fleet grows.

First Year Mandate

Spark deployments begin in early 2027. You will build the system before there is a fleet to run it on.

Stand up FRACAS, the root cause evidence standard, and the Failure Review Board.
Establish the as-built configuration baseline before there are units to reconcile.
Define spares, service intervals, and repair versus replace policy for the first generation.
Participate in the production release and ramp readiness reviews for the first deploying generation as the receiving organization.

What You'll Be Working On:

I. Fleet Ownership & Field Issues

Transfer of Ownership: Take technical ownership of each generation once it completes production ramp, through a defined handover from New Product Introduction covering the released configuration, open issues, and known risks.
Fleet Reliability: Own failure rate by subsystem, mean time between failures, and repeat failure rate, and define the telemetry every unit must report to make them measurable. Data Center Facility Operations owns uptime and time to repair.
Closed Loop Corrective Action: Run FRACAS and chair the Failure Review Board. Close every failure with a root cause, a verified fix, and proof it worked. A unit that fails while built within released tolerances is a design issue; attribution unresolved after ten business days proceeds as a Spark-funded fix and escalates to the Spark GM.
Containment: For safety or fleet-wide risk, contain first and settle attribution after. Own the retrofit decision and its sequencing.

II. Change, Configuration & Obsolescence

Post-Release Change Control: Own engineering change for generations in the field, with cost and fleet impact quantified before approval. New Product Introduction owns change control up to production release; you own it after.
Configuration Control: Own the configuration baseline and define what Operations records. Reconcile as-maintained against baseline so a change targets exactly the units that need it.
Obsolescence: Run a proactive DMSMS program. Model last time buys against fleet demand and qualify alternates before a shortage forces the choice.
Retrofit & Maintenance: Issue engineering change packages, kit definitions, preventive maintenance intervals, and acceptance criteria. Operations executes and returns the records; you verify effectiveness.

III. Feeding Product Management and NPI

Requirements into Product: Convert fleet evidence into quantified design requirements. Product Management decides what enters the PRD.
Qualification Requirements into NPI: Supply field-derived requirements and acceptance criteria, so a failure the fleet has already seen must be designed out and proven before the next generation is released.
Total Cost of Ownership: Own the reliability and service inputs to Spark unit economics.
Serviceability Advocacy: Represent serviceability and maintainability in design reviews. You hold no approval authority; you make the case with fleet data.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

Education

Required: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Reliability, or a closely related engineering discipline.

Experience

10 to 15 years in sustaining, reliability, or product support engineering for deployed capital equipment or infrastructure hardware.
Direct ownership of a fielded installed base, with field data converted into design change that measurably reduced failure rate or service cost.
Obsolescence and lifecycle management on a product whose service life exceeds that of the components inside it.
Experience standing a function up from nothing, including the processes and the partner agreements behind it.

Technical Depth

Reliability: FRACAS, structured root cause analysis, and mean time between failures and population failure rate analysis.
Change & Configuration: PLM, change order workflow, as-built control, and serial level effectivity.
Obsolescence: DMSMS practice, end of life monitoring, last time buy modeling, and alternate part qualification.
Systems Fluency: Electrical, mechanical, and thermal command sufficient to adjudicate root cause on a modular power and compute product, including liquid cooling.
Service Economics: Spares, service cost per unit, and the link between availability and revenue.

Additional Qualifications

Experience with modular, containerized, or prefabricated infrastructure products in the field.
Familiarity with liquid cooled data center hardware, including CDU and rack level cooling interfaces.
Mountaineer Spirit: The persistence to chase a root cause past the easy answer, and the judgment to know when a fleet-wide fix is worth its disruption.

Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

CURRENT PENN STATE EMPLOYEE (faculty, staff, technical service, or student), please login to Workday to complete the internal application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.
CURRENT PENN STATE STUDENT (not employed previously at the university) and seeking employment with Penn State, please login to Workday to complete the student application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.

Approval of remote and hybrid work is not guaranteed regardless of work location. For additional information on remote work at Penn State, see Notice to Out of State Applicants.

POSITION SPECIFICS

Your working location will be fully on-site located in State College, PA. This role requires periodic travel to remote locations.

We are searching for a Department Head for the Agile Systems Engineering Department (ASE) of the Materials, Manufacturing and Sustainment Office (MMSO) at the Applied Research Laboratory (ARL) at Penn State. The Agile Systems Engineering Department is dedicated to the application and training of systems engineering to support the advancement of warfighter capability at the speed of relevance. The department focuses on the rapid development of complex engineering systems requiring the integration of cross-disciplinary solutions and expertise, including system architecture design, functional analysis, requirements development, and model-based engineering. Additionally, the department has a lead role in workforce development and systems engineering training. This role will lead and manage all aspects of the Agile Systems Engineering Department, providing strategic direction, technical leadership, and operational oversight of a department of approximately 10 people. This leadership position requires a visionary leader capable of building and directing a multidisciplinary team focused on tailored application of systems engineering, model-based engineering, architecture development, and rapid, tailored systems integration. This position may be filled as either a Research and Development Engineer or a non-tenure Research Faculty.

ARL is an authorized DoD SkillBridge partner and welcomes all transitioning military members to apply.

You will:

Lead and manage all aspects of the Agile Systems Engineering Department, providing strategic direction, technical leadership, and operational oversight, personnel management, workforce planning, talent development, and performance evaluation
Build and direct a multidisciplinary team focused on the application of systems engineering to a diverse set of programs, technologies and sponsors
Mentor systems engineers in applying systems engineering to a variety of complex engineering problems that span levels of technical maturity ranging from early science and technology to system acquisition
Support division leadership in developing and maintaining relationships with sponsors in support of meeting funding objectives
Lead individual research projects and portfolios including developing technical concepts, writing winning proposals, staffing projects, conducting research, managing budgets, and delivering high-quality results
Foster partnerships with U.S. Military Program Offices, defense contractors, systems integrators, and other government laboratories
Lead department personnel in developing and delivering training on systems engineering to ARL staff and external partners
Foster a culture of innovation, technical excellence, and mission focus

Additional responsibilities for the higher-level position includes:

Support development of a comprehensive roadmap for embedded systems and integration methodologies pertinent to systems of interest to the division including but not limited to missiles, hypersonics, and uncrewed aerial systems
Establish and maintain partnerships with U.S. Military Program Offices, defense contractors, systems integrators, and other government laboratories
Build strategic relationships with Defense Industrial Base stakeholders
Collaborate across ARL departments and with external stakeholders as a trusted agent in identifying and applying appropriate systems engineering activities for large U.S. Military development programs

Required skills/experience areas include:

Leading individual research projects and portfolios including developing technical concepts, writing winning proposals, staffing the project, conducting the research, managing budgets, and delivering high-quality results
Past success applying systems engineering techniques for complex system development, with emphasis on streamlined and/or tailored processes
System architecture design, functional analysis, requirements development, system decomposition, and flow down of requirements
System and interface architecture development and testing
Evaluation of communications, messaging, and data architectures
Developing logical and physical representative models of system requirements and architectures
Developing time-varying physics-based models
Model-based approaches to supplement traditional test & evaluation (T&E) methods for more complete and cost-effective verification & validation of system requirements
systems engineering challenges in complex systems (e.g., maritime, aerospace, ground vehicles, unmanned systems)
Past success in writing white papers or reports
Active security clearance, at the Secret level or higher

Minimum Education, Work Experience & Required Certifications

If filled as R&D Engineer, Department Head (ARL) - Principal Professional, this position requires: Bachelor's Degree - Engineering or Science 19+ years of relevant experience Required Certifications: None If filled as R&D Engineer, Department Head (ARL) - Advanced Professional, this position requires: Bachelor's Degree - Engineering or Science 5+ years of relevant experience Required Certifications: None If filled as R&D Engineer, Department Head (ARL) - Senior Professional, this position requires: Bachelor's Degree - Engineering or Science 14+ years of relevant experience Required Certifications: None

ARL’s purpose is to research and develop innovative solutions to challenging scientific, engineering, and technology problems in support of the Navy, the Department of Defense (DoD), and the Intel Community (IC). FOR FURTHER INFORMATION on ARL, visit our website at
www.arl.psu.edu
.

Notice regarding employment at the Applied Research Laboratory (ARL): Employees must be eligible to obtain a government security clearance, participate in the ARL drug testing program, and comply with electronic and physical monitoring requirements applicable to federal contractors. ARL operates in a secure information environment involving Unclassified, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), and Classified information. Personal electronic devices brought onsite must be registered and may be restricted from certain areas. You must be a U.S. citizen to apply.

Our Team

Engage customer engineering teams supporting both networking and compute hardware specific to host (switch) to module (NIC card) cabling applications.
Identifies product and application trends/opportunities to drive next gen product roadmaps.
Engage in technical & technological sessions with key customers and internal teams.
Support architecture engineering to customized applications.
Establish partnerships with the industry eco system suppliers.

Experience in AI Rack architectures & future roadmaps.
Experience developing customer relationships at the leadership level
Experience communicating across all levels of business and executive leadership presence
Business acumen to deliver high level communication in the specified field

Collaborate with Application teams and tech leads in understanding cases and requirements

Drive capacity, scaling and hygiene requirements across all infrastructure components for the Apps
Closely collaborate with other squads across the fleet keeping user's requirements and delivery timelines in mind

Profound understanding of containerization technology and Kubernetes infrastructure
Experience working across multiple diverse technology and production teams
Experience in leading and reviewing work of Devops and python engineers
Knowledge of infrastructure: TLS and Certificates, scheduling, CI/CD tooling (Jenkins, Github

Deep understanding of Kafka
Hands-on experience in modern observability stack and modern authentication like oidc, mtls
Experience building and deploying distributed and multi-tenant systems
Experience in troubleshooting and debugging distributed production systems and code

Advanced Python Development
Knowledge of Flink is a plus
Java Development
Knowledge of modern storage and database technologies (MongoDB, MemSql, Snowflake, GPFS)
Knowledge of Electronic trading (equities, options, swaps) and trade lifecycle is a plus

new_jobs.title: Director, Engineering PMO
new_jobs.description:
Why Choose Us?

Novolex is a leading manufacturer of food, beverage, and specialty packaging that supports multiple industries including foodservice, restaurant delivery and carryout, food processing, grocery and retail, and industrial sectors. Novolex manufacturing and sourcing expertise spans a diverse range of substrates including resin, paper, molded fiber, aluminum and more. We provide customers a broad array of stock and customized solutions with 120 product categories, 250 brands and over 39,000 SKUs.

Our Sustainability Commitment

The Novolex sustainability vision is built upon three pillars: our products, our operations and our people. Each is critically important to our growth and future as a business. These pillars form the foundation of our company-wide commitment to sustainability, helping us achieve our ambitious goals through our wide-ranging initiatives.

Position Summary:

The Director, Project Management & Commercialization is responsible for leading the project management and commercialization function for engineering initiatives across Novolex Business Units. This role establishes the strategic direction for the team, advances standardized project management governance, and leads the implementation of an enterprise stage-gate process to strengthen execution discipline, improve visibility, and ensure alignment to business priorities.

Key Responsibilities:

Develop and execute the strategic roadmap for the Project Management & Commercialization team, including team mission, operating model, role clarity, and implementation priorities.
Operationalize the organization by establishing governance routines, decision-making protocols, operating rhythms, and cross-functional interfaces with Engineering, Operations, Commercial, Finance, and Business Unit leadership.
Design, standardize, and implement an enterprise stage-gate project management process, including gate criteria, approval requirements, required deliverables, escalation pathways, and performance metrics.
Lead change management and cross-business-unit implementation to drive adoption of project management standards, tools, reporting cadence, and governance expectations.
Own project schedules, budget tracking, and scope management to ensure deliverables meet quality standards and deadlines.
Oversee the end-to-end lifecycle of engineering projects, including balancing timelines, budgets, and technical specifications.
Assign tasks, balance workloads, and delegate responsibilities to maximize team productivity.
Act as the primary bridge between the engineering team and stakeholders.
Perform additional duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

Essential

10+ years of program management, project management, commercialization, PMO, or enterprise initiative leadership experience, preferably within a manufacturing or engineering environment.
5+ years of leadership experience leading engineering or technical organizations.
Experience developing and implementing project management strategies, governance models, stage-gate processes, or PMO capabilities within a manufacturing or engineering environment.
Demonstrated ability to establish operating rhythms, lead organizational change, and implement standardized processes across cross-functional stakeholder groups.
Strong management and prioritization skills.
Executive communication and stakeholder alignment capability.
Technical background and understanding of engineering principles and practices.
Experience overseeing multiple projects simultaneously, at multiple locations.
Ability to communicate cross-functionally with both internal and external stakeholders.
Proficiency using common office technology and tools.

Preferred

Experience supporting packaging, plastics, extrusion, thermoforming, molded fiber, paper, and/or related manufacturing operations.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related technical discipline highly preferred.

Travel:
Up to 50%

A reasonable estimate of the current range is $180,000- $200,000 + bonus + benefits. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target salaries for the position across all US locations. Within the range, individual pay is determined by job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. At Novolex, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

The benefits for this role include 401(k) plan with company match, comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, flexible spending and health savings accounts, paid vacation, and sick days, paid parental leave, paid holidays and wellness program.

What You'll Get From Us

Benefits

With safety as our top priority and a commitment to employee well-being an important focus, we offer comprehensive and competitive benefits that include medical, dental and vision insurance as well as a variety of other well-being resources focused on mental, physical and financial health. Specific benefits and well-being programs may vary depending on where you work.
Community Engagement
At Novolex, giving back to the local communities that support us is important. Our Focused Giving Program prioritizes support for organizations whose missions promote sustainability initiatives or address food and hunger needs. We also encourage facility level support of activities in the communities where our employees live and work.

Training and Development

We offer constant opportunities for advancement. From skills development to advanced education programs, training and development programs and courses are available through MyLearning. Programs include company and industry training curricula, support for formal education through the Tuition Reimbursement Program (Non-Union), and a Learning Management System that supports and enhances employee skills at all levels of the organization.

new_jobs.title: VP, Cloud and Infrastructure Engineering
new_jobs.description:
Job Description:

AssetMark is a leading strategic provider of innovative investment and consulting solutions serving independent financial advisors. We provide investment, relationship, and practice management solutions that advisors use in helping clients achieve wealth, independence, and purpose.

Position Summary

The Vice President of Cloud and Infrastructure Engineering is the senior leader responsible for the strategy, architecture, engineering, operations, reliability, and continuous improvement of AssetMark's cloud and infrastructure platforms.

This role owns the technology foundation that enables the business, including Azure Cloud, DevOps and platform engineering, Infrastructure as Code, databases, data platforms, enterprise networking, office connectivity, wireless, firewalls, SD-WAN, load balancing, F5, and Azure networking services.

The VP will also own the infrastructure foundation required to support AssetMark's AI strategy. This includes establishing the compute, data, networking, security, automation, governance, and operational capabilities needed to responsibly develop, deploy, and support AI-enabled solutions at scale.

This is a senior technical leadership position requiring strong executive presence, broad infrastructure experience, and sufficient technical depth to challenge designs, guide complex decisions, lead through major incidents, establish an engineering roadmap, and create measurable organizational change.

We can only consider candidates for this position who are able to accommodate a hybrid work schedule and are close to our Charlotte, NC office.

Primary Responsibilities

Cloud and Infrastructure Strategy: Define and execute a multi-year Cloud and Infrastructure Engineering strategy. Establish target-state architecture, platform standards, service ownership, production-readiness expectations, and a prioritized roadmap that balances reliability, modernization, security, automation, cost, AI adoption, and business growth.
Leadership and Team Development: Lead and develop a high-performing organization of technical leaders, cloud engineers, DevOps engineers, database professionals, network engineers, architects, and platform specialists. Establish clear accountability, career paths, technical standards, operating procedures, and succession plans.
Azure Cloud Platform: Own the design, operation, and continuous improvement of the Azure environment. Establish standards for landing zones, subscriptions, management groups, resource organization, naming, tagging, policies, access controls, compute, storage, networking, backup, monitoring, and resiliency.
Azure Networking and Platform Services: Define standards for Azure Virtual Networks, private endpoints, Private Link, VPN, ExpressRoute, Azure Firewall, Web Application Firewall, Application Gateway, Load Balancer, Front Door, DNS, and related services. Ensure cloud platforms are secure, scalable, highly available, recoverable, and operationally supportable.
DevOps and Platform Engineering: Lead the evolution of DevOps and platform engineering capabilities across technology teams. Establish source-control, CI/CD, artifact-management, release-automation, environment-promotion, platform-API, and self-service standards that improve developer experience while maintaining appropriate governance and controls.
Infrastructure as Code and Terraform: Make Infrastructure as Code the standard for provisioning and managing cloud and infrastructure services. Lead the adoption and governance of Terraform, including reusable modules, remote state, versioning, testing, code review, secrets management, drift detection, policy enforcement, and automated change promotion.
Database and Data Platform Engineering: Own the operational strategy and engineering standards for SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Snowflake, and related data platforms. Establish standards for architecture, performance, capacity, high availability, backup, recovery, patching, upgrades, monitoring, security, and lifecycle management. Partner with Data Engineering and Analytics teams to support reliable data services.
Network and Connectivity Engineering: Own the strategy and architecture for enterprise network services across offices, data centers, cloud environments, and remote users. Lead wired and wireless networks, firewalls, SD-WAN, VPN, WAN connectivity, DNS, IP address management, load balancers, F5, and Azure network services.
AI-Ready Infrastructure and Emerging Technology: Define the infrastructure strategy required to support enterprise AI adoption. Establish secure and scalable patterns for AI workloads across Azure, Snowflake, and other approved platforms, including compute, storage, networking, data access, APIs, GPU-enabled workloads, monitoring, capacity, security, and cost management. Evaluate emerging technologies and move practical capabilities from experimentation into production-ready services.
Security by Design: Embed security requirements into cloud, network, database, DevOps, AI, and infrastructure engineering practices. Partner with Cybersecurity and Identity and Access Management on Zero Trust, privileged access, vulnerability management, network segmentation, secrets management, identity-based controls, data protection, and secure third-party connectivity.
Reliability, Operations and Resilience: Establish an operational model for cloud and infrastructure platforms that includes observability, capacity planning, incident and problem management, change governance, disaster recovery, business continuity, backup, recovery testing, and service-level objectives. Partner with Service Resilience to improve end-to-end service health and reliability.
Automation and Continuous Improvement: Use PowerShell, Python, APIs, Terraform, Bicep, CI/CD, policy-as-code, and workflow automation to reduce manual work, configuration inconsistency, operational risk, and infrastructure-related tickets. Automate platform onboarding, environment management, compliance evidence, cost controls, and AI infrastructure patterns where practical.
Financial and Vendor Management: Own infrastructure financial planning, forecasting, FinOps, consumption management, and cost optimization across Azure, Snowflake, AI workloads, networking, licensing, and vendors. Manage strategic relationships, contracts, renewals, service performance, and commercial negotiations.
Cross-Functional Delivery: Partner with Service Resilience, Identity and Access Management, Cybersecurity, Applications, Data, Enterprise Architecture, Finance, Procurement, and business leaders to translate requirements into secure, scalable, resilient, automated, and adopted platform services.

Organizational Scope

The VP will lead through senior managers, technical leads, and engineering teams across the following capability areas:
Cloud and Platform Engineering: Azure platform services, landing zones, subscriptions, compute, storage, cloud operations, and platform standards.
DevOps and Developer Enablement: CI/CD, developer platforms, release automation, platform APIs, self-service, and engineering standards.
Infrastructure Automation: Terraform, Infrastructure as Code, policy-as-code, configuration management, automation, and platform lifecycle management.
Database and Data Platform Engineering: SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Snowflake, database operations, data platform reliability, and platform security.
Network and Connectivity Engineering: Office, wireless, WAN, SD-WAN, firewalls, F5, load balancing, remote access, and Azure networking.
AI Platform Enablement: Infrastructure patterns, operational readiness, security, governance, capacity, and cost controls for AI workloads.

Required Qualifications

Experience: Typically 15 or more years of progressive experience across cloud, infrastructure, engineering, operations, or technology platforms, with significant experience leading enterprise technology functions.
Leadership: Significant experience leading global technical teams, developing managers and engineers, building new capabilities, and directing delivery through a strategic roadmap.
Azure: Demonstrated ownership of enterprise Azure environments, cloud transformation initiatives, platform engineering, cloud governance, and production operations.
Terraform and Infrastructure as Code: Deep experience with Terraform and Infrastructure as Code at enterprise scale, including modules, state management, CI/CD integration, testing, policy enforcement, drift detection, and operational governance.
DevOps and Platform Engineering: Broad experience across DevOps, CI/CD, platform engineering, automation, developer enablement, observability, and production operations.

new_jobs.title: Director Systems Engineering, North America
new_jobs.description:
Director, Systems Engineering — North America

Title flexible to Senior Director or Field CTO for exceptional candidates

Location: United States (Remote / Field)

Travel: Around 25%, primarily to EBCs and customer sites in North America
Eligibility: Candidates must be US Citizens or US Permanent Residents.

Why This Role

You'll be RtBrick's first senior technical leader in the US: the primary technical interface between our engineering core and US customers, carrying carrier-grade software that is already in production into a market we're just entering. You start as the hands-on technical lead and build the systems engineering team as US accounts land.

About RtBrick

RtBrick builds the software that lets operators run their network edge the way cloud providers run data centers. Our platform, RtBrick Full Stack (RBFS), replaces monolithic, proprietary edge systems with cloud-native, disaggregated software that runs on Broadcom DNX-based white boxes and on cloud instances.
RBFS is a full Multiservice Edge (broadband network gateway, CGNAT, peering, aggregation and edge routing) on one software base built on open APIs.
RBFS is also built for AI-assisted operations. Every RBFS element includes an MCP server that lets AI agents diagnose and operate the network. Each agent action goes through the same authenticated, audited and reversible commit path as an operator's change, and humans approve what gets applied.
The software is proven in production. Deutsche Telekom has approved RBFS for deployment in its network, where it delivered a significant reduction in five-year total cost of ownership versus the incumbent approach. RBFS has carried subscriber and business traffic for years with service providers in Austria, Germany, Canada and Taiwan, through failures, upgrades and traffic peaks. Backed by major telco investors, we are now opening the US market.

The Role

You'll own the architecture conversation with US customers from the first whiteboard session through production deployment. You'll report to: Head of Professional Services.
The work is architectural. You'll design how operators move from monolithic edge platforms to disaggregated, cloud-native infrastructure: subscriber management at scale, CGNAT, peering and aggregation, and the IP/MPLS and BGP/EVPN designs underneath. You'll also help operators adopt AI-assisted operations without giving up control of their network.
The role demands range. You'll go deep with a customer's principal architects on routing design, then take the same conversation to the C-suite as a commercial and roadmap discussion, often in the same week.

What You'll Do

•
Customer-Facing Technical Authority. Serve as the lead architectural voice for US accounts. Lead technical workshops, design reviews (HLD/LLD), and complex POCs and make sure our solution meets each customer's network requirements.
•
Strategic Pre-Sales and Solution Design. Translate customer use cases (massive-scale access, DC interconnect, peering) into technical requirements for our engineering team. Own the technical win.
•
AI-Assisted Operations. Guide operators in adopting RBFS's built-in MCP server and agent-driven operations, from read-only diagnosis to human-approved and templated changes.
•
Product Evolution. Act as the Voice of the Customer. Work closely with the CEO, CTO, and Product Managers to prioritize features that solve real operator pain points, weighing long-term product vision against immediate market demands.
•
Team Leadership and Mentorship. Grow into building and managing a team of high-caliber Systems Engineers and Solutions Architects. Build an engineering-first culture that values deep hands-on skills alongside commercial acumen.
What Success Looks Like in Your First 12 Months
•
First US POCs designed, run, and converted into technical wins.
•
A US reference architecture for migrating from incumbent edge platforms to RBFS.
•
Field feedback reflected in the product roadmap through the Field and Product Management team.
•
The first Systems Engineering hires as US accounts land.
What You Bring: Required
•
Experience. 15+ years in service provider networking, with at least 5 years at Principal or leadership level.
•
IP/MPLS Edge Routing. Hands-on experience in IP/MPLS edge routing with fluency in Layer 2/3 protocols (BGP, IS-IS, OSPF, Segment Routing).
•
Service Provider Architecture. Expert understanding of large-scale service provider architectures (BGP/MPLS, Segment Routing, EVPN). Experience managing complex multi-vendor integrations and carrier-grade reliability requirements.
•
Cloud-Native Networking. Solid understanding of cloud-native networking (Kubernetes, microservices, APIs, NETCONF/YANG). Expertise in cloud-native or containerized NOS environments.
•
Hands-On Technical Credibility. While this is a director-level role, you must be comfortable diving into packet-level details, reviewing configurations, and navigating a Linux-based NOS.
•
Disruptor Mindset. Experience articulating the TCO and CapEx benefits of white-box, disaggregated models versus traditional chassis-based systems.
•
Communication. Proven ability to present complex technical roadmaps to CTOs and VPs, and to keep composure during high-stakes commercial or technical negotiations.
•
Drive. A can-do attitude. You thrive in a high-performance environment where autonomy is expected and pay for performance is the norm.
What You Bring: Preferred
•
Experience with CGNAT or Broadband Network Gateway (PPPoE/IPoE).
•
Familiarity with Broadcom-based merchant silicon and white-box hardware.
•
Experience at a disaggregated or challenger networking vendor, or inside an ISP or MSO.
Why RtBrick
•
Real impact. You'll build on software that already works at carrier scale, replacing legacy edge platforms in production networks today, not pitching a roadmap.
•
Hard problems. Subscriber management at millions of sessions, cloud-native operations on merchant silicon, and intent-based networking that actually ships. Engineering is hard, and it's why people stay.
•
Direct access. Flat structure, no layers between you and the decision. You'll work daily with founders and industry veterans who are still deep in the technical details and still write code.
•
Build it from the ground up. You'll define how the US practice runs, set the architecture standard for a new market, and build the team behind it.

new_jobs.description:
Role: Director / Principal / Practice Lead – Performance Engineering

Location: US Remote

Level: Director (hands-on)

Background: Strong consulting experience required/preferred

Role Overview

This is the senior performance engineering position for North America and serves as the deputy to the practice leader. The person will lead client conversations around performance engineering, shape and scope of engagements, and take primary responsibility for building the offerings and IP that the practice sells.
Digital experience and UX performance are also important areas, including Core Web Vitals, RUM, perceived performance, and the connection to accessibility.

Key Responsibilities

Offering & IP Creation:
Develop offering narratives, taxonomies, accelerators, maturity models, and capability materials from scratch.
Client Advisory:
Lead performance strategy, architecture reviews, engagement oversight, and escalations.
Pipeline & Solutioning:
Support presales, RFPs, scoping, estimating, and account expansion.
Delivery Ownership:
Provide technical direction, reviews, escalation support, and people management.

Must-Have Experience

Strong hands-on performance engineering expertise covering workload modeling, test strategy, bottleneck analysis, and tuning across application, database, and infrastructure layers.
Proven consulting experience scoping, estimating, and defending engagements with client leadership.
Demonstrated experience creating, not just delivering, an offering, accelerator, framework, methodology, or other capability asset. Candidates should be able to discuss/show their contribution.
Working knowledge of digital experience and UX performance, including Core Web Vitals, RUM, and front-end performance.
Experience working in an onshore/offshore delivery model.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Strong Plus

Cloud cost and performance optimization or FinOps collaboration
WCAG/accessibility standards familiarity
Performance work on packaged enterprise platforms such as SAP, Oracle, or MS365
Front-end and UX performance expertise
Observability and production performance experience, not just pre-production testing
Cloud cost and performance optimization or FinOps collaboration
Performance engineering on packaged enterprise platforms such as SAP, Oracle, or MS365
Familiarity with accessibility standards (WCAG)
Strong presales experience
